_note: PLAN.md 1: player colour is the ONLY thing that distinguishes one player from
another in v1, which makes this palette a legibility requirement rather than a
styling preference (PLAN.md 13.2 item 11).
SimPlayer.colour is an INDEX into this list, not a Color -- the sim carries no
view types, and the index is what rides the snapshot's player_state. ORDER IS
LOAD-BEARING: index 0 is player 1, index 1 is player 2, and so on, so entries
must never be reordered once a save or replay exists.
Eight entries for the eight players PLAN.md 3.1 budgets for at full scope.
HOW THESE WERE CHOSEN, 2026-08-14. Eight hues cannot all be told apart by hue
alone: red-green colour blindness (~8% of men) collapses red, orange, green and
yellow onto one axis, so those four have to be separated by LIGHTNESS instead.
Each colour therefore sits on a rung of a CIE L* ladder, with the four members
of each confusion family spread ~16 L* apart:
family        member    L*    hex
yellow-axis   red       45    #D50032
green     59    #00A344
orange    76    #FFAB00
yellow    92    #FFEB00
blue-axis     blue      36    #0043D6
violet    54    #B44DFF
cyan      84    #00E5FF
neutral       white    100    #FFFFFF
Pairs that sit close in L* (violet 54 / green 59, blue 36 / red 45) are always
in OPPOSITE families, so they separate on the blue-yellow axis, which every
form of colour blindness preserves. No pair is close in both.
SLOT ORDER IS PART OF THE DESIGN. Most matches are 1v1 or 2v2, so the first
four slots are the four most separable colours: blue, red, yellow, cyan. Every
pair among them is either on opposite axes or at least 39 L* apart. Green and
yellow -- the one genuinely risky pair -- are slots 3 and 5, so they never both
appear before a 5-player match.
THE SHADER'S BLEND MODE DECIDES WHETHER ANY OF THIS SURVIVES (PLAN.md A.6).
isobake currently MULTIPLIES the tint into the texture at bake time, and under
pure multiply white is a no-op (an untinted-looking player) and dark colours
crush the texture detail underneath. A.6 must therefore mix toward the colour
rather than multiply by it, or preserve the texture's luminance and take only
the hue -- otherwise this ladder arrives on screen compressed and two of these
read as the same muddy patch. See ASSET_MISSING.md 5.
Gaia-owned entities take NO tint. Some 0 A.D. wildlife actors declare a
playercolor alpha role anyway (vis.sheep does), so the shader must key off who
OWNS the entity, not off whether the sprite has a mask.
